sections.text:
Humans and animals do not learn vision from a fixed set of data: they move, interact, and learn from the visual consequences of their actions. Motivated by this developmental view, we study whether robots can improve visual learning by actively collecting experience through curiosity-driven interaction.

We introduce DySCOVER, a self-supervised framework for active robot visual learning. A robot observes RGB frames, learns a visual autoencoder that encodes and reconstructs them, and trains a recurrent world model to predict the next visual latent state conditioned on the current state and action.

The agent's policy is trained only with intrinsic rewards: reconstruction error encourages visually novel observations, while the world model's error encourages transitions whose consequences are not yet predictable.

This prediction error biases the policy toward more intricate trajectories that enrich the agent's set of experiences with observations beyond those encouraged by visual novelty alone. Our experiments conducted with robotic arms as the embodied agents show that adding predictive curiosity improves the vision model over using visual curiosity alone.

Across variations in initial conditions, experience capacity, embodiment, and scene content, adding predictive curiosity consistently improved visual learning. These results show that predictive curiosity can improve active visual learning beyond reconstruction-based curiosity alone.

summary.en: The paper introduces DySCOVER, a self-supervised framework for active robot visual learning. A robot learns a visual autoencoder from RGB frames and trains a recurrent world model to predict the next latent visual state from the current state and action. Its policy uses intrinsic rewards: reconstruction error favors visually novel observations, while prediction error favors transitions that remain difficult to predict. Robotic-arm experiments show improved visual learning over visual curiosity alone, with the authors reporting consistent gains across variations in initial conditions, experience capacity, embodiment, and scene content.
summary.zh: 论文提出 DySCOVER，一种用于主动机器人视觉学习的自监督框架。机器人从 RGB 图像学习视觉自编码器，并训练循环世界模型，根据当前状态和动作预测下一视觉潜在状态。策略仅由内在奖励训练：重建误差鼓励探索视觉新颖的观察，预测误差则鼓励探索尚难预测的状态变化。机械臂实验显示，加入预测好奇心比单独使用视觉好奇心更能提升视觉模型；在不同初始条件、经验容量、具身形式和场景内容下，作者报告这一改进持续出现。

sections.text:
World Action Models (WAMs) commonly couple video and action experts through dense, layer-wise Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) attention, exposing action prediction to irrelevant visual features while enforcing matched expert depths. This coupling hinders selective visual-feature use and introduces redundant computation.

We introduce Bridge-of-Experts (BoE), instantiated as BridgeWAM, which aggregates visual, language, and proprioceptive priors through 32 Latent Bridge Queries (LBQs) into a shared, limited latent space.

Joint video-action supervision lets action gradients guide the Video Expert toward representations better suited for action prediction, while the Action Expert learns to selectively retrieve task-relevant information through cross-attention.

Decoupling expert depths and reusing LBQs during action denoising yield a 5.06B model with a 30-layer Video Expert and a two-layer Action Expert, achieving 98.25% success on LIBERO and 72.24% pooled success on LIBERO-Plus, demonstrating effective task execution and strong generalization with an ultralight action head.

Ablations support joint representation adaptation and unified LBQ conditioning. Relative to Fast-WAM, BridgeWAM reduces single-sample inference FLOPs by 28.72% in simulation profiling and real-robot latency to 77.1 ms (a 2.47-fold speedup).

Qualitative experimental results further indicate preferential attention to target objects and task destinations across perturbations.

summary.en: The paper presents Bridge-of-Experts, instantiated as BridgeWAM, which combines visual, language, and proprioceptive priors through 32 Latent Bridge Queries. Joint video-action supervision guides the Video Expert toward action-suited representations, while cross-attention lets the Action Expert retrieve task-relevant information selectively. The authors report success results on LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus, and ablations support joint representation adaptation and unified query conditioning. Compared with Fast-WAM, simulation profiling reports lower single-sample inference FLOPs and real-robot experiments report reduced latency. Qualitative results indicate attention to target objects and destinations under perturbations.
summary.zh: 论文提出 Bridge-of-Experts 架构，并以 BridgeWAM 实现，通过 32 个潜在桥接查询汇聚视觉、语言和本体感觉信息。联合视频与动作监督使动作梯度引导视频专家形成更适合动作预测的表示，动作专家则通过交叉注意力选择任务相关信息。模型在 LIBERO 和 LIBERO-Plus 上报告了相应成功率；消融实验支持联合表示适配和统一查询条件。相对 Fast-WAM，仿真分析显示单样本推理 FLOPs 减少，实机延迟也降低；定性实验显示模型在扰动下更关注目标物体和任务目的地。

sections.text:
Aerial mobile manipulation requires unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to traverse heterogeneous environments such as indoor and outdoor domains, and connect navigation with subsequent physical interaction within the same trajectories.

Existing aerial benchmarks are typically confined to single-environment settings, limiting evaluation of agents across continuous environmental transitions. When interaction is evaluated, agents are often initialized near the target, leaving the transition from navigation to interaction largely unassessed.

This work introduces CrossFly, a benchmark for long-horizon interaction-oriented aerial mobility across heterogeneous environments. CrossFly contains 15K trajectories across more than 20 reconstructed scenes under a unified simulation and evaluation framework, covering Indoor, Outdoor, and Indoor$\leftrightarrow$Outdoor trajectories.

It further introduces Interaction Readiness Rate (IRR) to assess whether terminal navigation states provide suitable conditions for downstream interaction without assuming a specific manipulation policy.

Experiments with five representative aerial vision-language-action (VLA) agents and the proposed CrossFly-Agent show that Indoor$\leftrightarrow$Outdoor settings are more challenging than single-environment settings, with the highest success rate reaching 9.7% on unseen scenes.

A downstream manipulation case study further validates the relevance of interaction-oriented arrival to subsequent physical interaction. We hope CrossFly helps advance aerial embodied intelligence toward unified mobility and physical interaction in heterogeneous environments.

summary.en: The paper introduces CrossFly, a benchmark for long-horizon aerial mobility oriented toward interaction across heterogeneous environments. It contains 15K trajectories in more than 20 reconstructed scenes, covering indoor, outdoor, and indoor-to-outdoor transitions. The benchmark proposes Interaction Readiness Rate to assess whether a terminal navigation state is suitable for subsequent interaction without specifying a manipulation policy. Experiments involving five representative aerial vision-language-action agents and CrossFly-Agent find transition settings more challenging than single-environment settings; the highest success rate on unseen scenes is 9.7%. A downstream manipulation case study examines the relevance of interaction-oriented arrival.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 CrossFly，这是一个用于评估异构环境中长时程、面向交互的空中移动能力的基准，包含 15K 条轨迹和 20 多个重建场景，覆盖室内、室外及室内外转换。基准提出交互就绪率，用于衡量导航终点是否适合后续交互，而不指定操控策略。对五种代表性空中视觉语言动作智能体及 CrossFly-Agent 的实验显示，室内外转换场景比单一环境更具挑战性；未见场景的最高成功率为 9.7%。下游操控案例研究进一步检验了面向交互的到达状态与后续实体交互的相关性。

sections.text:
Humanoid parkour requires locomotion policies to coordinate whole-body dynamics across rapidly changing terrains such as stairs, gaps, slopes, and obstacles. Existing learning-based humanoid locomotion policies typically infer actions from current and historical observations, while the future evolution of the robot state is represented only implicitly.

Explicitly anticipating short-horizon state evolution is particularly beneficial for multiple terrains locomotion, where current actions must account for upcoming contact transitions and whole-body dynamics.

We present ParkourForme, a Transformer-based sequence modeling framework that reformulates humanoid locomotion as a future-conditioned decision-making problem. The current robot state queries historical sensorimotor trajectories through cross-attention, while a lightweight prediction head forecasts short-horizon future proprioceptive states.

The future states are predicted solely from historical observations and actions, with ground-truth future states used only as supervision targets, and are fused with temporal features to generate the current action without future-information leakage.

We evaluate ParkourFormer on a diverse multi-terrain humanoid parkour benchmark including stairs, gaps, slopes, rough terrain, and obstacle traversal. ParkourFormer achieves a 93.96% mean traversal success rate, compared with 90.49% for a vanilla Transformer and 87.16% for a MoE-MLP policy, while maintaining a single policy across all terrain types.

These results demonstrate that explicit future-state modeling significantly improves robustness and generalization for agile whole-body locomotion.

summary.en: The paper presents ParkourFormer, a Transformer sequence-modeling framework that treats humanoid locomotion as future-conditioned decision-making. The current state queries historical sensorimotor trajectories through cross-attention. A prediction head forecasts short-horizon future proprioceptive states using only historical observations and actions; ground-truth future states serve only as supervision targets, avoiding future-information leakage in current action generation. On a multi-terrain parkour benchmark covering stairs, gaps, slopes, rough terrain, and obstacles, the authors report a higher mean traversal success rate than the compared vanilla Transformer and MoE-MLP policies, using one policy across terrain types.
summary.zh: 论文提出 ParkourFormer，一种将人形机器人运动表述为未来条件决策问题的 Transformer 序列建模框架。当前状态通过交叉注意力查询历史传感运动轨迹，预测头仅依据历史观察和动作预测短期未来本体感觉状态；真实未来状态只作监督目标，再与时序特征融合生成当前动作，以避免未来信息泄漏。在涵盖楼梯、间隙、斜坡、粗糙地形和障碍物的基准评估中，作者报告其平均通过成功率高于所比较的 Transformer 和 MoE-MLP 策略，并由单一策略处理所有地形。

items.title: ParkourFormer: Integrating Predictive Supervision and Sequence Modeling into Parkour Locomotion

sections.text:
Bilateral teleoperation with force feedback is becoming increasingly important, and the quality of external-torque estimation is critical to this process. However, manufacturer-provided disturbance-torque estimates on commercial robotic arms are often inaccurate, while the use of end-effector force/torque sensors adds cost and payload.

We propose LETS, a physics-guided learning approach that assigns rigid-body dynamics to recursive Newton-Euler inverse dynamics and reserves learning for only the robot-specific residual.

LETS uses only the robot's URDF model and joint feedback, deliberately excluding control commands and thereby decoupling external-torque estimation from control-command inputs. It trains on 12 minutes of free-motion data in under one minute, without requiring a dedicated end-effector six-axis force/torque sensor.

In bilateral teleoperation, LETS achieves real-time external-torque estimation that enables stable force feedback. Its free-space error is 69% lower than the manufacturer-provided estimate, substantially reducing coupled oscillations between leader and follower; its contact error is 28% lower, yielding more accurate haptic feedback.

summary.en: The paper presents LETS, a physics-guided learning method for external-torque estimation in bilateral teleoperation. It assigns rigid-body dynamics to recursive Newton–Euler inverse dynamics and learns only a robot-specific residual. LETS uses the robot’s URDF model and joint feedback, excluding control commands and requiring no end-effector six-axis force/torque sensor. It trains on 12 minutes of free-motion data in under a minute. The authors report real-time estimates enabling stable force feedback, with 69% lower free-space error and 28% lower contact error than the manufacturer estimate, as well as reduced coupled oscillations.
summary.zh: 论文提出 LETS，一种用于双边遥操作外部力矩估计的物理引导学习方法：用递归牛顿—欧拉逆动力学表示刚体动力学，仅学习机器人特定残差。方法仅使用 URDF 模型和关节反馈，不依赖控制指令或末端六维力/力矩传感器，并以 12 分钟自由运动数据在不到一分钟内训练。作者称其可实时估计力矩并支持稳定力反馈；在双边遥操作中，自由空间误差较厂商估计低 69%，接触误差低 28%，并减少主从端耦合振荡。

items.title: LETS: Low-Overhead External-Torque Sensing for Force-Feedback Bilateral Teleoperation

sections.text:
Model-based reinforcement learning has shown superior sample efficiency by leveraging the learned latent dynamics either in the form of derivative-free planning/imagined rollout training or dynamics gradient-based policy updates.

While these approaches achieve comparatively fast learning, they all suffer, to varying degrees, from issues of recurrent compounding errors, high inference-time latency, and instability in backward propagation through time (BPTT).

In this work, we propose a model-based RL approach that uses the chunk world model as a differentiable training-time evaluator to optimize the chunk actor without recurrent model invocation.

Through the collaborative chunk-wise prediction of the world model and policy, we can generate H-step hypothetical rollouts in a single forward pass and directly optimize value expansion, avoiding the costly and unstable BPTT.

We evaluate our method on 19 challenging high-dimensional humanoid tasks from HumanoidBench and deploy our method to the real-world for quadruped bipedal walking. Project Website: https://song-wx.github.io/cmpo.github.io/

summary.en: The paper proposes a model-based reinforcement learning approach that uses a chunk world model as a differentiable training-time evaluator for optimizing a chunk actor, without recurrent model invocation. The authors state that collaborative chunk-wise prediction by the model and policy generates H-step hypothetical rollouts in one forward pass and directly optimizes value expansion, avoiding costly and unstable backpropagation through time. They evaluate the method on 19 high-dimensional humanoid tasks in HumanoidBench and deploy it for real-world quadruped bipedal walking. The abstract does not specify the evaluation results.
summary.zh: 论文提出一种基于分块世界模型的模型式强化学习方法，将该模型用作可微的训练时评估器，以优化分块策略，避免循环调用模型。作者称，世界模型与策略协同分块预测，可在一次前向计算中生成 H 步假设轨迹并直接优化价值扩展，从而避免代价高且不稳定的时间反向传播。论文在 HumanoidBench 的 19 项高维人形机器人任务上评估，并将方法部署到现实世界的四足机器人双足行走任务；摘要未说明具体评估结果。

sections.text:
We completely characterize the solvability profiles of tasks for two autonomous mobile robots in the plane under variable disorientation, chirality, and rigid movements. The four standard capability models and the schedulers considered here have a known quotient order Q of thirteen computational classes.

A task's solvability profile is the set of classes in which it is solvable, and is necessarily an upset of Q. We prove that every upset is realizable and construct a minimum exact disjunctive basis of thirteen concrete tasks. The basis contains one task for each principal upset.

For every antichain of Q, the disjunction of the corresponding tasks has profile exactly equal to the union of their profiles. This exactness is not implied by the individual profiles: an algorithm may satisfy different disjuncts in different executions.

We establish it by constructing, for every algorithm in each maximal class outside the target union, a single admissible fair execution violating all selected predicates simultaneously.

Consequently, the realizable profiles form the entire finite distributive lattice Up(Q): there are exactly 54 profiles, counted by the antichain polynomial 1 + 13z + 24z^2 + 16z^3, and each has a canonical disjunctive representation using at most three principal tasks.

We also identify six tasks whose solvability signatures recover every inclusion and incomparability in Q, and prove that six is minimum even among arbitrary separating tasks. Their profiles are precisely the principal upsets generated by the join-irreducible elements of Q.

In contrast, any task family generating every profile by exact disjunctions must contain all thirteen principal profiles. Thus our exact disjunctive basis has minimum size and is unique at the profile level.

summary.en: The paper characterizes task solvability profiles for two autonomous mobile robots in the plane under varying disorientation, chirality, and rigid-movement capabilities. The authors describe a quotient order Q with 13 computational classes; each task profile is an upset of Q, and they prove every upset is realizable using a minimum exact disjunctive basis of 13 concrete tasks. The realizable profiles form the finite distributive lattice Up(Q), with 54 profiles, each representable using at most three principal-upset tasks. They also show that six tasks are necessary and sufficient to distinguish all inclusions and incomparabilities in Q, while exact disjunctive generation of every profile requires all 13 principal profiles.
summary.zh: 论文研究平面内两台自主移动机器人在方向感知、手性和刚体运动能力不同条件下的任务可解性。作者称，相关计算类别构成含 13 类的偏序 Q，每项任务的可解性轮廓是 Q 的上闭集；所有上闭集均可实现，并由 13 个具体任务构成最小精确析取基。由此，可实现轮廓组成有限分配格 Up(Q)，共有 54 种，每种都可用至多三个主上集任务表示。论文还称，六项任务足以且为最少，用于区分 Q 中所有包含与不可比关系；精确析取生成全部轮廓则必须包含全部 13 个主轮廓。

sections.text:
We introduce HelpMeOut, an embodied AI benchmark for error-aware monitoring of household task execution. Existing embodied household benchmarks typically assume that humans execute tasks correctly, but this assumption does not hold for cognitively impaired persons or older adults whose everyday activities produce structured execution errors.

To address this gap, HelpMeOut operationalizes research on everyday action errors into 20000 paired activity episodes, covering nine neuropsychologically motivated error categories.

In each episode, agents observe a streaming human activity trajectory and must monitor whether the execution is unfolding correctly, diagnosing any structured errors as early as possible. We evaluate learned-monitor, symbolic, change-point, and frontier LLM prompting baselines.

Results show that these methods perform poorly as error monitors, often missing when execution goes wrong. These results suggest a gap left by standard goal-inference and task-completion benchmarks, making HelpMeOut a testbed for error-aware assistive agents.

summary.en: The paper introduces HelpMeOut, an embodied AI benchmark for monitoring errors during household task execution. It addresses the assumption in many existing benchmarks that people perform tasks correctly, and operationalizes everyday action errors in 20,000 paired activity episodes across nine neuropsychologically motivated categories. Agents observe streaming human activity trajectories and must detect whether execution is going wrong and diagnose structured errors as early as possible. The study evaluates learned-monitor, symbolic, change-point, and frontier LLM-prompting baselines. The authors report that these methods perform poorly as error monitors and often miss execution errors, indicating a gap in standard goal-inference and task-completion benchmarks.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 HelpMeOut，这是一个面向家庭任务执行错误监测的具身人工智能基准。它针对现有基准通常假定任务执行正确的问题，整理了 20000 组配对活动片段，涵盖九类受神经心理学研究启发的错误。智能体观察连续的人类活动轨迹，需要尽早判断执行是否出错并诊断结构化错误。研究评估了学习式监测器、符号方法、变化点方法和前沿大语言模型提示基线；作者报告这些方法作为错误监测器表现较差，常会漏掉执行偏差，并据此指出现有目标推断和任务完成基准存在覆盖缺口。

sections.text:
Reliable robot autonomy requires reasoning about the world from partial and noisy observations. However, many perception systems model only visible scene regions, rely on fixed semantic categories, and assume reliable sensor measurements. These assumptions break under occlusion, novel object encounters, and sensor degradation.

In this paper, I present a research vision for incompleteness-aware scene understanding. I organize this vision around three fundamental challenges: incomplete evidence, incomplete knowledge, and incomplete sensor reliability.

I discuss my research contributions toward addressing these challenges through amodal perception, semantic occupancy forecasting, open-world scene understanding, label-efficient learning, and uncertainty-guided multi-modal fusion. Building on these contributions, I outline future research directions toward belief-centric 4D scene representations.

These representations aim to jointly model geometry, semantics, motion, and uncertainty. I also discuss active sensing and safe adaptation strategies that allow robots to reduce uncertainty through interaction. The goal is to develop calibrated and actionable scene representations that support reliable autonomy in dynamic, open-world environments.

summary.en: This research vision organizes incomplete scene understanding for robot autonomy around incomplete evidence, incomplete knowledge, and uncertain sensor reliability. The author discusses contributions in amodal perception, semantic occupancy forecasting, open-world scene understanding, label-efficient learning, and uncertainty-guided multimodal fusion. Future directions include belief-centric 4D scene representations that jointly model geometry, semantics, motion, and uncertainty, along with active sensing and safe adaptation. The stated goal is calibrated, actionable representations that support reliable autonomy in dynamic, open-world environments.
summary.zh: 这篇研究愿景文章将机器人场景理解中的不完整性归纳为证据、知识和传感器可靠性三方面，并讨论作者在非模态感知、语义占据预测、开放世界场景理解、标签高效学习及不确定性引导的多模态融合方面的研究贡献。作者提出未来发展以信念为中心的四维场景表示，联合建模几何、语义、运动与不确定性，并讨论主动感知和安全适应策略。其目标是形成经过校准且可用于行动的表示，支持动态开放环境中的可靠自主运行。

sections.text:
Vision-language model (VLM) agents can control robots through visual feedback and action primitives, but repeated LLM calls and redundant observations incur substantial token overhead.

We introduce PyRUA-Lean, an interactive code-execution framework in which the agent composes robot primitives, including vision-language-action (VLA) policies, into Python cells that check and retry locally and return only the images and state they request.

Across 700 simulated task instances from LIBERO-PRO, RoboTwin 2.0, and RoboCasa365, it raises success from 63.1% to 71.7% over tool calling with the same GPT-6 Astra planner and primitives, using 49% fewer LLM calls and 65% fewer input tokens on jointly solved instances.

On RoboDojo, without any VLA policy or privileged information, it reaches 51.6% average success rate (Score 58.2), 19.4 points above the top entry of the public leaderboard.

Based on the PyRUA-Lean framework, we train PyRUA-Lean Coder v0.1-4B, an open 4B model, with GRPO on 45 LIBERO-PRO instances; it improves from 18.8% to 44.1% on unseen task instances, surpassing the Qwen3.5-27B base model.

summary.en: The paper introduces PyRUA-Lean, an interactive code-execution framework where an agent composes robot primitives, including VLA policies, into Python cells that check and retry locally and return requested images and state. Across 700 simulated instances from LIBERO-PRO, RoboTwin 2.0, and RoboCasa365, the abstract reports higher success than tool calling with the same planner and primitives, alongside fewer calls and input tokens. On RoboDojo, the reported result uses no VLA policy or privileged information. A trained open 4B model also improves on unseen task instances.

sections.text:
Task planning for robots in off-site construction prefabrication is primarily manual, leading to planning inefficiencies and reluctance to adopt robotic solutions. Existing approaches provide limited support for scalable, modular automated task planning and localized runtime replanning.

This paper proposes APTree, a model-driven framework that integrates automated task planning with modular task execution using behavior trees as the execution model. APTree repeatedly applies and coordinates heterogeneous symbolic planners to automatically generate and compose modular task plans at runtime.

To support this approach, we develop a domain-specific language for the formal specification and validation of task plans, together with a compatible execution engine.

We evaluate APTree on the real-world livMatS Biomimetic Shell pavilion, where it models the construction robotic fabrication domain, detects injected specification and planning errors at design time and runtime, and automatically generates large-scale task plans by coordinating three symbolic planners across numerous planning modules.

A machine-checked formal analysis further shows that composed execution and local replanning are safe under explicitly stated assumptions, including planner soundness and non-interference of generated plans, providing practitioners with explicit conditions for dependable plan composition.

APTree thus enables construction practitioners to leverage automated task planning without requiring detailed knowledge of symbolic planning techniques or APTree's internal implementation.

summary.en: The paper presents APTree, a model-driven framework for construction robot task planning. It uses behavior trees for modular execution and coordinates heterogeneous symbolic planners to generate and compose plans at runtime. The framework includes a domain-specific language for specifying and validating plans and a compatible execution engine. Evaluation on the real-world livMatS Biomimetic Shell pavilion reports error detection and large-scale plan generation. A machine-checked analysis establishes safety of composed execution and local replanning under stated assumptions, including planner soundness and plan non-interference.
summary.zh: 论文提出APTree，一种面向施工机器人任务规划的模型驱动框架，使用行为树执行模块化计划，并在运行时协调多种符号规划器生成和组合计划。框架包含用于任务计划形式化描述与验证的领域专用语言及配套执行引擎。作者在livMatS仿生壳亭的真实建造场景中评估系统，报告其可检测设计时和运行时错误，并生成大规模计划。机器检查的形式分析表明，在规划器可靠、计划互不干扰等明确假设下，组合执行和局部重规划是安全的。

Assistance in collaborative manipulation is often initiated by user instructions, making high-level reasoning request-driven. In fluent human teamwork, however, partners often infer the next helpful step from the observed outcome of an action rather than waiting for instructions.

Motivated by this, we investigate an event-driven formulation of proactive assistance, where human--object interaction outcomes initiate assistive reasoning without user-provided task specifications at inference time.

To this end, we propose an event-driven framework that monitors workspace state changes with an event monitor and, upon event completion, extracts stabilized pre/post snapshots that characterize the resulting state transition.

A frozen pretrained Vision-Language Model (VLM) then uses its semantic priors to infer the task context, decide whether assistance is appropriate, and, when needed, generate a sequence of assistive actions from the observed transition.

To make outputs executable and verifiable, we restrict actions to a set of action primitives and reference objects via integer IDs. We evaluate the same framework across three distinct real world tabletop collaboration tasks without task-specific training or fine-tuning.

The event-driven framework achieves performance comparable to variants given user instructions.

summary.en: The paper investigates event-driven proactive robot assistance, in which changes resulting from human-object interactions trigger reasoning without user-provided task specifications at inference time. An event monitor extracts stabilized before-and-after workspace snapshots. A frozen pretrained vision-language model infers task context, decides whether assistance is appropriate, and generates assistive action sequences. Actions are restricted to primitives and objects are referenced by integer IDs. Across three distinct real-world tabletop collaboration tasks, without task-specific training or fine-tuning, the framework performs comparably to variants given user instructions.

Humanoids increasingly demand lightweight leg mechanisms for agile, dynamic, and energy-efficient locomotion. Reducing distal inertia through proximal actuation has thus become a common design goal. Yet, compact transmissions that preserve torque capability and efficient force transmission remain hard to achieve.

This paper presents a novel series-parallel leg design combining a knee parallel mechanism, an ankle parallel mechanism, and a nonlinear knee-ankle coupling where all actuators placed closer to the hip.

As the knee flexes, the coupling passively assists ankle dorsiflexion for foot clearance and, as it extends it assists plantarflexion for push-off, redistributing ankle load through the knee transmission. We derive the coupling's nonlinear transmission models and validate them in simulation and on hardware.

The design shows that the shared transmission lets both joints draw on each other's actuator capacity by easing the knee's peak torque demand under load and the ankle's peak speed demand during fast motion. %Together With the leg's proximal actuator placement, the leg achieves an effective reflected mass of 0.37kg at the foot for a 6kg leg, demonstrating very low distal leg inertia for dynamic humanoid robots.

summary.en: The paper presents a series-parallel leg mechanism for humanoids, combining knee and ankle parallel mechanisms with a nonlinear knee-ankle coupling and actuators placed near the hip. During knee flexion, the coupling assists ankle dorsiflexion for foot clearance; during extension, it assists plantarflexion for push-off and redistributes ankle load through the knee transmission. The authors derive nonlinear transmission models and validate them in simulation and on hardware. They report that the shared transmission lets the joints draw on each other's actuator capacity, easing peak knee torque demand under load and peak ankle speed demand during fast motion.

sections.text:
Semantic scene understanding has enabled robots to reason and perform affordance-driven object interaction. Despite this, real-world manipulation remains fundamentally limited by the inability to predict how objects move and are articulated. Long-horizon mobile manipulation requires closing the gap between semantics, geometry, and kinematics.

In this work, we present MoMa-SG, a novel framework for building semantic-kinematic 3D scene graphs of articulated scenes containing a myriad of interactable objects. Given RGB-D sequences containing multiple object articulations, we temporally segment object interactions and infer object motion using occlusion-robust point tracking.

We lift point trajectories to 3D and estimate articulation models using a novel unified twist estimation formulation that robustly estimates revolute and prismatic joint parameters in a single optimization pass. Next, we associate objects with articulations and detect contained objects by reasoning over parent-child relations at identified opening states.

We also introduce the Arti4D-Semantic dataset, which provides parent-child relation annotations between container and contained objects together with object axis annotations across 62 in-the-wild RGB-D sequences containing 600 object interactions and three distinct observation paradigms.

We extensively evaluate the performance of MoMa-SG on two datasets and ablate key design choices of our approach. In addition, real-world experiments on both a quadruped and a mobile manipulator demonstrate robust manipulation of articulated objects in everyday home environments. We provide code and data at: https://momasg.cs.uni-freiburg.de.

summary.en: The paper presents MoMa-SG, a framework for building semantic-kinematic 3D scene graphs of articulated scenes with interactable objects. From RGB-D sequences, it segments interactions, infers motion with occlusion-robust point tracking, lifts trajectories to 3D, and estimates revolute and prismatic joints using a unified twist formulation. It associates objects with articulations and identifies contained objects from parent-child relations at opening states. The authors introduce the Arti4D-Semantic dataset with annotations from in-the-wild sequences. They evaluate MoMa-SG on two datasets and report real-world articulated-object manipulation experiments with a quadruped and a mobile manipulator.

sections.text:
Efficient perception is a prerequisite for the small, low-power devices targeted by robotics, mixed reality, autonomous driving, and drone applications, all of which rely on Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) to estimate their motion within their surroundings.

Learning-based SLAM systems achieve state-of-the-art accuracy but are demanding in compute, whereas classical geometry-based methods retain a strong efficiency advantage with little to no loss in accuracy. In this work we present RootSLAM, a fully-featured visual-inertial SLAM system for multi-camera setups built on Basalt.

RootSLAM achieves accuracy competitive with the state of the art while running up to 20 times faster, facilitating the deployment of perception systems in resource constrained environments.

We adapt the square-root bundle adjustment formulation from structure from motion into the multi-camera visual-inertial SLAM setting through a novel reformulation that leverages the system's pose-graph, letting the global optimizer run in single-precision floating point, thus doubling its performance.

We provide a thorough benchmark against the state of the art together with an ablation study of our contributions. Our new implementation, including its map management and loop detection module, pose-graph optimizer, and global mapping components, will be open-sourced.

summary.en: The paper presents RootSLAM, a multi-camera visual-inertial SLAM system built on Basalt. It adapts square-root bundle adjustment to this setting through a reformulation that uses the pose graph and enables single-precision global optimization. The authors report accuracy competitive with the state of the art and runtime up to 20 times faster. They also describe benchmark comparisons and an ablation study, and state that the implementation will be open-sourced.
summary.zh: 论文提出 RootSLAM，一种基于 Basalt、面向多相机配置的视觉惯性 SLAM 系统。作者将平方根束调整改写到多相机视觉惯性 SLAM 中，并利用位姿图使全局优化器能够采用单精度浮点运算。作者称该系统精度可与先进方法竞争，运行速度最高快 20 倍；还报告了基准比较和消融研究，并表示实现将开源。

sections.text:
Articulated object manipulation tasks such as opening doors, tightening bolts, and pulling drawers impose kinematic constraints on a robot end-effector's motion that neural policies may fail to satisfy.

Unlike hybrid force-position control that strictly separates force and position control into orthogonal subspaces, impedance control modulates a mechanical impedance system in the form of a virtual inertia, damping, and stiffness. However, selecting task-appropriate impedance gains remains challenging for robot policies.

In this paper, we address this problem for the case of manipulating articulated objects. Our constraint-decomposed impedance control method uses the sampling diversity of a generative policy to estimate the feasible motion directions in twist space.

The key idea is to infer the feasible and constrained subspaces of twists from an ensemble of trajectories generated by the policy from the same observation. Principal component analysis (PCA) of the end-effector twists determines the feasible twist subspace, which is then used to form 6x6 impedance gain matrices.

For many common articulated objects, the feasible twist subspace is independent of the object configuration, so the subspace and resulting gains are estimated once and held fixed during manipulation, minimizing computational overhead.

For less common cases where this independence does not hold, we instead estimate a configuration-independent twist subspace of higher dimension that contains the local feasible subspaces, allowing the same fixed-gain strategy to be used.

Experiments across simulated and real-world single- and multi-DoF objects show that the proposed method consistently reduces constraint-violating contact loads relative to isotropic impedance control while maintaining task execution.

summary.en: The paper proposes constraint-decomposed impedance control for articulated-object manipulation. It estimates feasible end-effector twist directions from multiple trajectories generated by a policy for the same observation, then uses them to form impedance gain matrices. For common objects, the estimated subspace can remain fixed; other cases use a higher-dimensional fixed subspace containing local feasible subspaces. Experiments on simulated and real single- and multi-degree-of-freedom objects show reduced constraint-violating contact loads relative to isotropic impedance control while maintaining task execution.
summary.zh: 论文提出用于铰接物体操作的约束分解阻抗控制方法，从生成策略针对同一观测产生的多条轨迹中估计末端执行器扭转运动的可行子空间，并据此构造阻抗增益矩阵。对于常见物体，估计出的子空间可固定使用；其他情形则采用包含局部可行子空间的较高维固定子空间。仿真和真实物体实验显示，该方法相较各向同性阻抗控制降低了违反约束的接触载荷，同时保持任务执行。

sections.text:
World-action models (WAM) predict future states to guide robot actions, enabling learning from both action-free video and action-labeled interaction. Most inherit pretrained video generators, leaving WAM pretraining and scaling underexplored.

We introduce Genie Envisioner Act 2.0 (GE-Act 2.0), a world-action model whose trainable generative and action components are all initialized from scratch on manipulation data. It combines a control-oriented autoencoder (CoAE), a single-step visual planner (SVP), and an inverse dynamics model (IDM).

CoAE retains action- and instruction-relevant information under aggressive compression, while SVP produces a complete future state in one differentiable pass, so visual planning and inverse dynamics can be pretrained separately on complementary data.

The components are then jointly trained with knowledge-aligned selective optimization (KASO), which reduces mismatched supervision by selecting only predicted futures judged behaviorally compatible with the recorded action.

We evaluate pretrained checkpoints directly, without per-task fine-tuning, on 100 tasks across 20 manipulation skill groups with held-out scenes, backgrounds, lighting, and object instances.

Scaling co-training data from 300 to 30,000 hours raises success from 17.1% to 44.1% on G1-OP and from 13.4% to 31.1% on G2-90D; despite comprising less than 2% of the co-training data, G2-90D improves by 17.7 points, suggesting cross-embodiment transfer.

Gains span 19/20 and 18/20 skill groups, and skill-specific coverage strongly correlates with zero-shot out-of-distribution (OOD) success (Pearson r=0.80; Spearman rho=0.85).

Under the same protocol, the model grounds object, color, shape, and position references in at least 90% of trials and follows explicit instructions even when they conflict with an already-committed behavior or a conventional scene association.

summary.en: The paper presents GE-Act 2.0, a world-action model whose trainable generative and action components are initialized from scratch on manipulation data. It combines a control-oriented autoencoder, a single-step visual planner, and an inverse dynamics model. The components are pretrained separately, then jointly trained with selective optimization intended to reduce mismatched supervision. In evaluations without task-specific fine-tuning across 100 tasks, the authors report higher success with more co-training data, gains across most skill groups, and a correlation between skill coverage and zero-shot out-of-distribution success. The model also follows references to object properties.

sections.text:
During human-robot interaction, sight plays an important role. When the human sees a robot, they can observe the robot's actions and better predict the robot's future behaviors. Conversely, when the human cannot see the robot, they become uncertain about the robot's intent and plans. In this paper, we focus on the human's field of view.

Existing human-aware planners either ignore this field of view and assume the human can observe the entire scene, or intentionally design their interactions so the robot is always visible to the human. By contrast, we enable robots to infer what the human has and has not seen during interaction, i.e., the human's field of view.

We then apply this estimate as a vision-aware filter on the robot's actions. Given a nominal robot policy and a model of the interaction, we roll out the policy over a short horizon to see how the robot's state updates.

We then reweight the actions based on how those actions impact the robot's predicted visibility: higher weights are assigned to actions that bring the robot into (or away from) the human's line of sight.

In practice, our framework provides an online estimation and filtering process that repeatedly updates its understanding of the human's field of view and then locally perturbs robot actions based on the human's vision. We evaluate our vision-aware filter on robots that assist humans in collaborative cooking and coordinate with them in driving environments.

Across simulations and a 12-participant user study, we find that our vision-aware filter changes both performance and preference: participants completed over three times as many subtasks with in-view assistance while cooking, and had fewer collisions with cars that purposely stayed out of their view while driving.

summary.en: The paper presents a vision-aware filter that lets a robot estimate online whether a person can see it, then adjust actions according to predicted visibility. It rolls out a nominal policy over a short horizon and reweights actions based on their effect on the robot’s visibility. The authors evaluate the method in collaborative cooking and driving scenarios through simulations and a 12-participant user study. They report over three times as many subtasks completed with in-view assistance during cooking, and fewer collisions with cars that deliberately remained outside participants’ view while driving.
summary.zh: 本文提出一种面向人机交互的视觉感知过滤器，使机器人在线估计人是否看得到自己，并据此调整动作。方法将名义策略在短时域内展开，按预测可见性重新加权动作。作者在协作烹饪和驾驶场景中进行仿真及12人用户研究，报告称烹饪时参与者在机器人处于视野内获得帮助后完成的子任务超过三倍；驾驶时，故意留在人类视野外的车辆与参与者发生的碰撞较少。

Teleoperation is widely used to collect high-quality demonstrations for robot learning. Dexterous manipulation, however, requires coordinated control of motion and contact forces. Operators can specify motion, but struggle to reproduce the subtle force adjustments of human manipulation without feeling the robot's contacts.

We introduce Force-Modulated Dexterity (FOMO-Dex), a unified compliance formulation for contact-rich manipulation. FOMO-Dex expresses nominal actions in coordinates defined by task geometry and contact structure. It applies force-driven motion corrections along selected directions while leaving the remaining command components unchanged.

Across card picking, paper cutting, screwdriving, and nut-and-bolt assembly, FOMO-Dex reduces excessive contact forces compared with stiff control. A user study shows that operators collect more successful demonstration data per hour after brief practice.

For policy learning, imitating the corrected actions improves card-picking success over imitating raw operator commands. Policies trained on FOMO-Dex demonstrations also achieve more rotation in nut-and-bolt manipulation and screwdriving than those trained on demonstrations collected with the stiff controller.

Videos are shown on https://yingyuan0414.github.io/fomo-dex/ .

summary.en: The paper introduces FOMO-Dex, a unified compliance method for contact-rich manipulation. It represents nominal actions using task geometry and contact structure, applies force-driven motion corrections along selected directions, and leaves other command components unchanged. Across card picking, paper cutting, screwdriving, and nut-and-bolt assembly, the authors report reduced excessive contact forces compared with stiff control. A user study found that operators collected more successful demonstrations per hour after brief practice. Policies trained on corrected demonstrations improved card-picking success and achieved more rotation in nut-and-bolt manipulation and screwdriving.

sections.text:
Most existing approaches rely on video or motion-capture data for reinforcement learning (RL) training; however, all of these methods require an upper-level module to generate reference trajectories in real time.

In object carrying tasks, the humanoid can only lift objects from designated locations along the reference trajectory, resulting in poor spatial generalization. Moreover, existing policies can only be evaluated inside a motion-capture studio.

To address these limitations, we propose \textbf{MOVER}, a multi-stage, Teacher-Assistant-Student, RL training framework for humanoid object carrying. We first collect data from videos and employ GENMO and GMR to retarget the video data, combining this with data augmentation techniques to generalize the data across objects of varying shapes and sizes.

In the \textbf{first stage}, building upon the DeepMimic \cite{peng2018deepmimic} motion-training framework, we train the humanoid to transport objects from specified locations along designated trajectories.

In the \textbf{second stage}, we relax the tracking of the reference motion and adjust the reward so that the humanoid learns to transport objects from different positions. In the \textbf{third stage}, we apply a Dagger-PPO distillation method to distill away the proprioceptive position observations and reference joint position of the humanoid.

This allows the deployed policy to operate without relying on global position information from a motion-capture system; instead, the humanoid can directly perceive the object's pose from its onboard RGB-D camera to complete the carrying task.

We design a series of simulation experiments to compare the success rates across stages (Stages 1 vs. 2) and before versus after distillation. We further transfer the policy to a real humanoid, successfully transporting objects at varying positions in a motion-capture-free setting.

summary.en: The paper proposes MOVER, a staged teacher-assistant-student reinforcement learning framework for humanoid object carrying from human video. Video motions are retargeted and augmented to cover objects of varied shapes and sizes. Training progressively relaxes reference-motion tracking, then distills away dependence on global position and reference joint-position observations. The deployed policy uses an onboard RGB-D camera to perceive object pose. The authors design simulation experiments to compare stages and performance before and after distillation, and report transferring the policy to a real humanoid that carried objects from varying positions without motion capture.
summary.zh: 本文提出 MOVER，一种分阶段的师生强化学习框架，旨在使人形机器人从人类视频中学习可泛化的搬运任务。方法将视频动作重定向并扩增，以覆盖不同形状和尺寸的物体；随后逐步放宽参考动作跟踪，并通过策略蒸馏移除对全局位置和参考关节位置的依赖。部署策略使用机载 RGB-D 相机感知物体姿态。作者设计仿真比较不同训练阶段及蒸馏前后的成功率，并报告已将策略迁移至真实人形机器人，使其在无需动作捕捉系统的环境中搬运不同位置的物体。

sections.text:
Pose Graph Optimization (PGO) is a classical and widely applied problem in state estimation for robotics, playing a fundamental role in localization, mapping, and navigation. Yet, it is nonconvex in nature and may have many local minimizers, thus difficult to analyze.

In this paper, we investigate the optimization landscape and establish a sufficient condition of global optimality for PGO. The ultimate goal of this paper is to theoretically confirm that the optimization landscape is benign and attractive around the global minimizer, if noise is smaller than an explicit and a priori bound.

To reveal such an insight, this paper develops three main technical results. First, we identify a proper basin of attraction (BOA) containing global minimizer, and characterize its geometric property by showing that its radius is controlled by noise in an explicit way.

Then, by exploring the first order optimality conditions of PGO, we prove that a local minimizer is globally optimal if a noise-controlled criterion is satisfied.

Finally, by combining above two results, we prove that one and only one local minimizer exists in the BOA and this minimizer is globally optimal, when the noise is smaller than an explicit bound that can be verified a priori.

Numerical simulations validate the proposed theory under various random cases, showing that the obtained conditions provide an effective criterion for certifying the global optimality of PGO.

summary.en: The paper studies the optimization landscape of pose graph optimization (PGO) and establishes sufficient conditions for certifying global optimality when noise is below an explicit, a priori verifiable bound. It identifies a basin of attraction containing the global minimizer and shows that its radius is explicitly controlled by noise. A criterion derived from first-order optimality conditions establishes when a local minimizer is globally optimal. Combining these results, the authors prove that below the noise bound, the basin contains exactly one local minimizer, which is globally optimal. Random numerical simulations validate the theory and the criterion’s effectiveness.
summary.zh: 本文研究位姿图优化（PGO）的优化景观，并提出在噪声低于可事先验证的明确界限时，判定全局最优性的充分条件。作者定义包含全局极小值的吸引域，并证明其半径受噪声显式控制；还依据一阶最优条件给出局部极小值为全局最优的噪声相关判据。结合两项结果，作者证明满足噪声界限时，吸引域内恰有一个局部极小值，且该点为全局最优。随机数值仿真用于验证理论条件及其认证效果。

sections.text:
Learning humanoid loco-manipulation from human demonstrations rests on observing how locomotion, posture, and object interaction evolve together as tasks unfold. Scaling collection across diverse environments, in turn, favors lightweight, portable capture systems. Yet, existing datasets provide only partial views of this coordination.

Thus, we introduce EgoExplorer, a 100-hour vision-motion-touch observatory of human loco-manipulation built with a wearable system.

With an emphasis on professional activities, its continuous recordings align egocentric video with reconstructed whole-body motion, fine-grained finger articulation, and tactile observations, accompanied by step-level descriptions. To achieve this coverage with sparse body sensing, we develop the Calibrate-Complete-Constrain pipeline.

Concretely, reusable calibration fixes participant geometry and sensor attachments before motion inference to disentangle mounting offsets from articulation.

A temporal prior then completes unobserved joint motion, while layered constraints promote measurement agreement, temporal continuity, and geometric consistency, properties that motion plausibility alone does not guarantee.

Against tracker-fitted references, the method reduces body-point error by 71.9% relative to the strongest baseline; matched evaluations also show gains in hand stability and contact estimation. Preliminary studies explore multimodal generation and conditioning alongside humanoid retargeting with whole-body control in simulation.

summary.en: The paper presents EgoExplorer, a wearable observatory for human loco-manipulation that aligns egocentric video with reconstructed whole-body motion, finger articulation, tactile observations, and step-level descriptions. Its Calibrate-Complete-Constrain pipeline calibrates participant geometry and sensor attachments, completes unobserved joint motion, and applies measurement, temporal, and geometric constraints. The authors report reduced body-point error against tracker-fitted references, alongside gains in hand stability and contact estimation. Preliminary studies explore multimodal generation and conditioning, and humanoid retargeting with whole-body control in simulation.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 EgoExplorer，这是一个通过可穿戴系统采集的人类移动与操作数据集，持续记录第一人称视频、重建的全身动作、手指关节和触觉信息，并配有步骤级描述。作者提出 Calibrate-Complete-Constrain 流程，用于校准传感器与参与者几何关系、补全未观测关节动作，并施加测量、时间和几何约束。与跟踪器拟合参考相比，作者报告身体点误差降低；初步研究还探索了多模态生成、条件控制及仿真中的人形机器人动作重定向。

items.title: EgoExplorer: A Vision-Motion-Touch Observatory for Human Loco-Manipulation In Situ

sections.text:
Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) predict masked or future observations in representation space, offering a natural source of predictive latents for vision-language-action (VLA) models.

Yet making these latents useful across pretraining, policy learning, and deployment requires addressing three failures: mismatch with embodiment-specific control, interference with action learning, and teacher miscalibration under distribution shifts.

We introduce Juno, a unified framework built around one action-conditioned JEPA that serves as a control-aligned representation backbone, a predictive teacher, and an adaptable dynamics model. During pretraining, we train it on embodiment-matched trajectories and use a dynamic CLS loss to transfer motion-weighted patch dynamics to a compact global state.

During policy learning, we fuse current-frame JEPA patches into VLA perception and use a decoupled reasoning branch with separate transformation parameters to distill future latent states for action generation.

During deployment, we adapt the world model on all observed transitions, including failed rollouts, freeze the adapted teacher, and re-align the policy on verified executions using LoRA adapters and a trainable action head, without expert corrections or task rewards.

On SimplerEnv, Juno raises average success from $60.9\%$ to $68.5\%$ over Qwen3GR00T, the strongest baseline, and test-time adaptation further reaches $72.7\%$; on a real robot, it retains $70\%$--$75\%$ success under background, height, and object shifts where the base policy collapses to $0\%$.

summary.en: The paper introduces Juno, a framework that uses one action-conditioned joint-embedding predictive architecture as a representation backbone, predictive teacher, and adaptable dynamics model for vision-language-action policies. It trains on embodiment-matched trajectories, distills future latent states through a decoupled reasoning branch, and adapts at deployment using observed transitions before re-aligning the policy on verified executions. The authors report higher average success than the strongest baseline on SimplerEnv, with further gains from test-time adaptation. On a real robot, they report retained success under background, height, and object shifts where the base policy collapses.
summary.zh: 论文提出 Juno，将一个动作条件化的联合嵌入预测架构用于视觉语言动作模型的表示、预测教师和动力学模型。预训练阶段使用与具身匹配的轨迹和动态 CLS 损失；策略学习阶段融合当前帧特征，并通过独立推理分支蒸馏未来状态；部署阶段则利用观察到的转移适配模型，再以已验证执行重新对齐策略。作者报告，在 SimplerEnv 上成功率高于 Qwen3GR00T 基线，测试时适配后进一步提高；真实机器人测试中，在背景、高度和物体变化下仍保持一定成功率，而基础策略失效。

items.title: Juno: Taming Predictive Latents for Vision-Language-Action Models

sections.text:
We present CoPlanVLM, which uses a Vision Language Model (VLM) to translate a single natural-language instruction and image into coordinated paths for a team of two robots. While VLMs offer a flexible, natural-language interface for commanding robot teams, their weak spatial reasoning has greatly limited VLM-based path planning.

CoPlanVLM improves the VLM's spatial reasoning and path planning abilities through three components: （1） an image overlay marking both free space and obstacles, （2） task classification that selects the most appropriate low-level planner and reasoning prompt for each instruction, and （3） task-specific chain-of-thought reasoning that prompts the VLM to identify key objects, allocate roles, and verify routes are collision-free before committing to a plan.

Together, these components enable the team to complete complex coordinated maneuvers requiring both robots and divide large tasks between robots to increase efficiency. CoPlanVLM also supports detailed maneuvers involving specific routes, loops, and coverage of large areas, as well as tasks requiring directional reasoning such as north/south or left/right.

We validate CoPlanVLM in both Gazebo simulation and on physical Turtlebot 4 hardware. CoPlanVLM attains an average success rate of 84.4% compared to 50.0% for the closest baseline. On trials where both methods succeed, CoPlanVLM's paths are 27% shorter on average. Project code is available at https://github.com/AICPS/CoPlanVLM.

summary.en: The paper presents CoPlanVLM, which converts a natural-language instruction and an image into coordinated paths for two robots. It improves spatial planning through an image overlay of free space and obstacles, task-based selection of a low-level planner and prompt, and task-specific reasoning to identify objects, assign roles, and check routes for collisions. The authors evaluate the system in Gazebo simulation and on physical Turtlebot 4 hardware. They report an average success rate of 84.4%, compared with 50.0% for the closest baseline; when both methods succeed, CoPlanVLM paths are 27% shorter on average.
summary.zh: 论文介绍 CoPlanVLM，根据一条自然语言指令和一张图像，为两台机器人生成协同路径。方法通过标注空闲区域与障碍物的图像叠加层、按任务选择低层规划器及提示，以及引导模型识别关键物体、分配角色并检查路线是否无碰撞，来改进空间推理。作者在 Gazebo 仿真和实体 Turtlebot 4 上验证，报告平均成功率为 84.4%，对比基线为 50.0%；在两种方法均成功的试验中，CoPlanVLM 路径平均短 27%。

sections.text:
Despite rapid progress, generalist robot policies remain brittle during execution. Reliable deployment therefore requires runtime monitoring that provides timely warnings of failure. Existing monitors commonly estimate risk from current observations or policy signals without explicitly predicting the future consequences of proposed actions.

To anticipate such risks before action execution, we introduce ReAP, a future-aware runtime monitoring framework that combines visual failure recognition with action-conditioned failure prediction. Specifically, ReAP first trains a visual detector on successful and failed rollouts to learn a failure-relevant representation space and estimate current risk.

An action-conditioned predictor then forecasts the resulting future representation in this space to estimate future failure risk. At runtime, the detector and predictor provide complementary signals for current-state failure recognition and future-aware risk assessment.

Experiments across diverse robot policies in simulation and the real world demonstrate that ReAP effectively balances failure-detection accuracy and warning timeliness.

summary.en: The paper introduces ReAP, a runtime monitoring framework that combines visual failure recognition with action-conditioned prediction to warn of robot policy failures. A detector trained on successful and failed rollouts learns a failure-relevant representation and estimates current risk. A predictor then forecasts the future representation conditioned on a proposed action to estimate future failure risk. At runtime, the two components provide complementary signals for recognizing current failures and assessing upcoming risks. Experiments across diverse robot policies in simulation and the real world are reported to balance detection accuracy with warning timeliness.
summary.zh: 论文提出 ReAP，一种面向机器人运行时监控的未来风险预测框架，结合视觉失败识别与动作条件化预测。系统先用成功和失败轨迹训练视觉检测器，以学习与失败相关的表示并估计当前风险；随后预测器根据拟执行动作预测未来表示，从而估计未来失败风险。运行时，检测器和预测器分别提供当前状态失败识别与前瞻风险评估信号。作者称，在仿真和真实世界的多种机器人策略实验中，ReAP 能兼顾失败检测准确性与预警及时性。

items.title: ReAP: From Visual Failure Recognition to Action-Conditioned Risk Prediction for Runtime Failure Monitoring

sections.text:
An LLM-directed excavator can execute mechanically feasible motion whose destination or authority no longer matches the operator's approval. We propose execution-bound authorization for the approval--dispatch--execution interval.

A one-use lease binds the action, generated motion, mission contract and admission tolerance; atomic dispatch rechecks current authority and measured joint drift. Periodic supervision detects revocation and requests a quintic stop with a carry-pitch endpoint, selected through sampled joint, stroke, flow and reference-acceleration checks.

The framework connects exact motion identity to dispatch integrity and load-aware interruption. Evaluation combines a 672-case interface suite, four loaded digging cases in synchronous simulation, unloaded MuJoCo/Pinocchio transfers and two command-level LLM planners.

The gateway admitted all 120 benign interface cases and produced zero unauthorized dispatches in the attack suite. Loaded dispatch-window tests produced zero unauthorized deposition. During simulated dump-phase revocation, maximum closed-site deposition decreased from 1.23 to 0.33\,m$^3$; loaded-slew stops used less than 75\% of nominal swing torque.

These results demonstrate motion-bound authorization and quantify the retention and stopping behavior of supervised excavation skills.

summary.en: The paper proposes execution-bound authorization for excavators, using a one-use lease to bind an approved action, generated motion, mission contract, and admission tolerance. Dispatch rechecks authority and joint drift, while supervision detects revocation and requests a sampled-check stop. Evaluation covers interface tests, loaded digging in synchronous simulation, unloaded simulation transfers, and two command-level LLM planners. The authors report no unauthorized dispatches in the attack suite and reduced closed-site deposition during simulated revocation.
summary.zh: 论文提出面向挖掘机执行过程的授权框架，以一次性租约绑定获批动作、生成运动、任务约定和准入容差，并在派发时重新核验权限与关节漂移；运行中监督撤销并请求经采样检查的停止动作。评估包括接口测试、同步仿真中的载荷挖掘、无载荷仿真迁移和两种命令级大语言模型规划器。作者报告，接口套件中的良性请求全部获准，攻击套件未发生未授权派发；仿真撤销测试降低了封闭区域沉积量，载荷摆转停止使用的摆转力矩低于额定值的75%。

sections.text:
State-of-the-art perceptive humanoid locomotion is mostly built on retargeted motion capture, a generative motion prior, and a distillation stage. We report a complete system that does not require this pipeline for a humanoid to cross varied terrain.

In its place, we provide a five-expert mixture routed by a terrain classifier over a sensed elevation grid, and target every foothold with a model-based planner, refined by six closed-form-gradient steps on an interpolated terrain-cost field instead of picked from a fixed grid.

Driven through the same perception-to-actuation software a robot would run, inside a second, deployment-fidelity simulator, it crosses an $85$\,m five-segment waypoint course $18$ of $20$ times end-to-end ($90\%$, Wilson $95\%$ CI $70$--$97$) and succeeds $20/20$ on four of five segments scored alone, where an ablated configuration without the mixture and without refinement reaches $0\%$ on both the stair and the hurdle segment.

The continuous refinement moves $72.4\%$ of foot placements across at least one grid-cell boundary, which produces real sub-grid correction.

We also ran matched component studies to report what does not account for it: one expert equals five on the training distribution, four label-free routers collapse to near-uniform activation, and a self-supervised terrain embedding loses to the privileged label.

summary.en: The paper reports a humanoid terrain-traversal system that does not require retargeted motion capture, a generative motion prior, or distillation. A terrain classifier routes a five-expert mixture, and a model-based planner selects footholds that are refined with closed-form gradient steps on a terrain-cost field. In a deployment-fidelity simulator, the system completed an 85-meter, five-segment course 18 of 20 times; four segments scored alone achieved 20 of 20. Ablations and component studies are also reported.
summary.zh: 论文报告了一套不依赖运动捕捉重定向、生成式运动先验或蒸馏流程的人形机器人越野系统。系统使用由地形分类器路由的五专家混合模型，并通过模型规划器选择落脚点，再以地形代价场上的闭式梯度步骤细化。在部署保真度仿真器中，系统在五段路线中端到端成功18/20次；单独评分时，五段中的四段达到20/20。去除专家混合与细化的消融配置在楼梯和跨栏段成功率为零。作者还报告了组件对照研究及落脚位置发生跨网格单元变化的比例。

sections.text:
We present a learning-based framework that enables a full-scale bipedal humanoid to sprint at over 7 m/s with motion-prior-guided gait and perform aggressive cornering at high speed with a pronounced trunk lean of up to $25^\circ$.

Achieving this combination is challenging: above approximately 4 m/s, periodic foot impacts induce severe, high-frequency yaw-rate oscillations intrinsic to high-speed gaits.

This high-frequency temporal structure corrupts the history of proprioceptive feedback that flat-MLP policies rely on, while rendering conventional yaw-rate tracking rewards counterproductive, as they fight against the robot's natural oscillatory dynamics.

Moreover, a single style prior shared across skills cannot tell which skill is commanded and inherently compromises the low-speed skill fidelity. To overcome these limitations, we adopt a causal multi-head attention (MHA) module to explicitly model the high-frequency temporal feedback.

In place of the oscillatory yaw rate, we design a heading-direction reward that supervises only the low-frequency velocity direction, allowing agile turning at high speed without suppressing natural gait oscillations.

We further introduce skill-conditioned multi-adversarial-motion-prior (MAMP) discriminators that condition the style reward on the commanded skill.

Ablation experiments confirm that each mechanism is essential: replacing structured temporal encoding with a flat-history MLP caps the top speed; reverting to yaw-rate tracking prevents high-speed turning; and a single shared discriminator makes in-place turning collapse into a quasi-static stance.

Our framework bridges the gap between raw sprinting speed and reference-motion fidelity, demonstrating stable high-speed sprinting and aggressive cornering in both simulation and real-robot deployment.

summary.en: The paper presents a learning framework for a full-scale bipedal humanoid, reporting sprint speeds above 7 m/s and aggressive high-speed cornering in simulation and real-robot deployment. It uses causal multi-head attention to model high-frequency proprioceptive feedback, a heading-direction reward instead of yaw-rate tracking, and skill-conditioned motion-prior discriminators. Ablation experiments report that removing these mechanisms limits top speed, prevents high-speed turning, or causes in-place turning to collapse into a quasi-static stance.

sections.text:
Evaluating robot manipulation policies through repeated physical trials is costly. We study whether an action-conditioned world model can serve as a closed-loop test environment whose policy success rates track those on real robots.

Beyond realistic video, the model must return the camera views and proprioceptive state needed for the policy's next action and preserve failed-action outcomes to avoid overestimating policy capability. We introduce ProWorld, a world model that jointly predicts multi-view video and robot state, then feeds both back to a frozen policy for repeated interaction.

ProWorld comprises a shared transformer for joint video-state flow prediction and Shared-Time View Encoding to distinguish cameras while preserving temporal synchronization.

To reduce interaction hallucinations that turn missed grasps into successful lifts, we augment training with failed interactions collected in high-fidelity simulation, reducing inflated success rates in the generated environment. ProWorld achieves the highest overall TriWorldBench score among the compared methods.

Across three policies and four local manipulation tasks, it attains a Pearson correlation of 0.95 and a Spearman correlation of 0.94 between generated and real success rates. These results support joint visual-proprioceptive feedback and failure-aware training as a basis for world-model-based policy evaluation.

summary.en: The paper studies whether an action-conditioned world model can evaluate manipulation policies in a closed loop, with simulated success rates tracking real-robot results. ProWorld jointly predicts multi-view video and robot state and feeds both to a frozen policy for repeated interaction. Training includes failed interactions collected in high-fidelity simulation to reduce hallucinated successful lifts after missed grasps. The authors report the highest overall TriWorldBench score among compared methods and correlations of 0.95 (Pearson) and 0.94 (Spearman) across three policies and four tasks.

sections.text:
LLM agents increasingly control robots using VLA policies, perception models, and procedural knowledge. These modules are difficult to reuse because their interfaces, embodiment assumptions, and conditions of use differ, and their benefits on physical tasks remain unclear.

We package them as embodied skills that extend agent skills with explicit embodiment assumptions and conditions of use, building 250 action, perception, and experience skills from 1,052 resources. On this basis we introduce EmbodiedSkillBench, which runs an agent in a closed observation-action loop and records success, actions, tokens, and wall-clock time.

It supports three modes: native control, skill-only execution, and Agent-Directed Reuse (ADR), a mode we propose in which the agent keeps its native controls and decides for each skill whether to invoke, modify, or ignore it.

Across four agents on 100 perturbed LIBERO-Pro tasks, we find that skills help an agent only as far as they exceed what it can already do. Skill-only execution lifts GPT-5.6-Sol from 11% to 63% and Kimi-K3 and Claude-Opus-5 by about 20 points, while cutting their token usage by 58% to 85%.

Yet all four agents then end up between 61% and 64%, and GPT-6-Astra falls from 92% under native control to 61%.This suggests that as agents grow stronger, the role of embodied skills shifts from supplying missing capability to reducing cost: GPT-6-Astra already solves most tasks through native control, so restricting it to skills removes more than it adds.

Under ADR, which lets it keep native control and call skills selectively, GPT-6-Astra recovers to 85%, within 7 points of native control, while using 14.1% fewer tokens and 11.9% less time. With Jev as a skill choosing motion directions and gripper actions, it reaches 81% with 50% fewer tokens and 57% less time.

The code is available at https://github.com/HanZhi306/EmbodiedSkill-Bench.

summary.en: The paper introduces EmbodiedSkillBench to evaluate embodied skills on physical tasks and describes a collection of action, perception, and experience skills. The benchmark compares native control, skill-only execution, and agent-directed reuse, where an agent chooses whether to invoke, modify, or ignore each skill. On 100 perturbed LIBERO-Pro tasks across four agents, the authors report that skills help when they add capabilities the agent lacks. Skill-only execution improves some agents but constrains a stronger one; selective reuse recovers much of its performance while reducing token use and time.

sections.text:
We present a low-cost miniature Ackermann vehicle for embedded neural-driving research, organized as a hardware-partitioned perceive-decide-act agent: an ESP32 camera node streams frames over Wi-Fi to a host computer, where neural inference and state estimation run, while an ESP32-S3 chassis controller executes safety-critical actuation in a 100 Hz per-wheel proportional-integral-derivative (PID) loop beneath a micro-ROS client.

The partition isolates real-time control and safety on the vehicle while learning-based components run off-board, supervised by an operator from a gamepad. We characterize the complete pipeline during real closed-loop neural driving.

Wireless sensing, rather than neural inference, dominates latency, with a 59.5 ms median capture-to-actuation delay; the platform absorbed wireless variability by holding the last safe command under a firmware watchdog, operating across twelve autonomous sessions with zero collisions or manual interventions; and encoder-inertial-measurement-unit (IMU) fusion cut odometry loop-closure error by 22%.

These results indicate that carefully partitioned microcontroller-class vehicles support reproducible experiments in embedded AI, wireless control, and operator-supervised autonomous driving. The platform software is open source.

summary.en: The paper presents a low-cost miniature Ackermann vehicle for embedded neural-driving research. Its hardware partition places camera sensing and chassis control on separate microcontrollers, while neural inference and state estimation run on a host computer; an operator supervises driving with a gamepad. The authors characterize the complete pipeline during real closed-loop driving. They report that wireless sensing dominates latency, that the vehicle completed twelve autonomous sessions without collisions or manual intervention, and that encoder-IMU fusion reduced odometry loop-closure error. They position the platform for reproducible experiments in embedded AI and wireless control.

sections.text:
Pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policies provide strong language-conditioned manipulation knowledge, but they remain largely vision-driven and can struggle once manipulation enters contact states where the scene is occluded, depth is ambiguous, or small force errors push execution off the offline demonstration distribution.

We present LIFT (Late Reactive Injection of Force for VLA Post-Training), a force-aware post-training framework that adds contact reactivity to a pretrained VLA policy while preserving its output at initialization.

LIFT grafts a reactive action expert beside the original action expert, initializes it from pretrained action weights, and injects recent 6D end-effector force through causal force memory and zero-initialized cross attention, enabling actions to be refreshed during execution.

To address the policy-dependent distribution shift of contact feedback, LIFT further couples reactive force injection with an online DAgger loop that trains on a mixture of offline task-alignment data and human-corrected online rollouts.

Across towel folding, book insertion, and Hanoi ring placement, LIFT learns faster and reaches higher peak and final performance than vision-only DAgger, while ablations show that reactive force memory and online corrective data are both important for robust contact-rich manipulation. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/y-wng/lift

summary.en: The paper presents LIFT, a post-training framework that adds force reactivity to a pretrained vision-language-action policy. It places a reactive action expert beside the original expert and injects recent six-dimensional end-effector force through causal force memory and zero-initialized cross-attention, allowing actions to be refreshed during execution. An online DAgger loop combines offline task-alignment data with human-corrected rollouts to address distribution shifts from contact feedback. On towel folding, book insertion, and Hanoi ring placement, the authors report faster learning and higher peak and final performance than vision-only DAgger. Ablations indicate that both force memory and online corrective data contribute to robust contact-rich manipulation.

sections.text:
World action models (WAMs) have emerged as an important class of generalist robot policies, aiming to transfer video prediction priors to action learning. However, we find that existing WAMs frequently produce incorrect motion predictions in open-ended environment, leading to erroneous actions.

We attribute this limitation to two factors: （1） base video models are not optimized for manipulation, and （2） naively incorporating action components into video models can substantially degrade their generalization capabilities.

We introduce Video Prediction Policy 2 (VPP2), a WAM that enables strong zero-shot generalization in both video prediction and action generation. First, we curate a large-scale, diverse dataset of manipulation videos to continue pretraining the base video foundation model.

We annotate video clips with detailed captions and perform \textit{event-level} video pretraining to promote generalization across open-ended manipulation tasks. Second, we post-train and distill the video model into a single-step visual planner with fixed prediction horizon.

Finally, we introduce action module via a mixture-of-transformers (MoT) architecture to learn implicit inverse dynamics model.

Experiments demonstrate three key results: （1） VPP2-14B outperforms Cosmos3-64B by 11.0\% points in video prediction instruction-following success rate on open-ended tasks; （2） VPP2 surpasses the strongest baseline by 18.5\% points in success rate on real-world zero-shot ALOHA manipulation tasks; and （3） following benchmark-specific post-training, VPP2 achieves the highest success rates among evaluated methods on the challenging LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-OOD, and RoboDojo benchmarks.

sections.text:
Human-robot collaboration (HRC) in structured assembly requires reliable state estimation and adaptive task planning under noisy perception and human interventions. To address these challenges, we introduce a design-grounded human-aware planning framework for human-robot collaborative structured assembly. The framework comprises two coupled modules.

Module I, Perception-to-Symbolic State (PSS), employs vision-language models (VLMs) based agents to align RGB-D observations with design specifications and domain knowledge, synthesizing verifiable symbolic assembly states. It outputs validated installed and uninstalled component sets for online state tracking.

Module II, Human-Aware Planning and Replanning (HPR), performs task-level multi-robot assignment and updates the plan only when the observed state deviates from the expected execution outcome. It applies a minimal-change replanning rule to selectively revise task assignments and preserve plan stability even under human interventions.

We validate the framework on a 27-component timber-frame assembly. The PSS module achieves 97% state synthesis accuracy, and the HPR module maintains feasible task progression across diverse HRC scenarios.

Results indicate that integrating VLM-based perception with knowledge-driven planning improves robustness of state estimation and task planning under dynamic conditions.

sections.text:
VLMs provide promising solutions to embodied reward design. Most current methods that train VLMs as reward regressors not only require extensive annotations but are also primarily designed for finetuning pretrained policies, and perform less well in the more challenging from-scratch RL setting.

This issue stems from a fundamental mismatch: regressing precise rewards is misaligned with what VLMs naturally excel at.

We posit that it is more aligned with VLMs' inherent multi-modal VQA capabilities for the models to function as success detectors, and propose VLM success reward via Exploration-Augmented Key-Observation Gating (VLMeg) to well harness VLM for embodied reward design.

As the core of VLMeg, the proposed exploration-augmented key-observation gating first determines whether the current RL episode is judgment-worthy based on its similarity to a generated success trajectory. Then, the key observation with the lowest confusion from the judgment-worthy episode will be selected for VLM evaluation as episodic reward.

This gating mechanism not only avoids redundant calls but also enables higher detection accuracy of VLM.

Considering the sparsity of judgment-worthy episodes, the advanced exploration incentives based on the generated trajectory are introduced, enabling more efficient exploration toward judgment-worthy trajectories for more VLM reward triggers and thus gaining higher RL efficiency.

Extensive experiments in MetaWorld demonstrate VLMeg achieves state-of-the-art from-scratch RL, outperforming advanced VLM-based baselines on 12 challenging reward-free tasks. Furthermore, VLMeg also enables effective RL without any ground-truth reward in 3 challenging real-world experiments.

Code will be open after acceptance at https://github.com/Raina915/VLMeg.

summary.en: The paper proposes VLMeg, which uses a vision-language model as a success detector for embodied reinforcement learning rather than as a precise reward regressor. It assesses whether an episode is suitable for judgment based on similarity to a generated success trajectory, selects a key observation with low confusion for model evaluation, and adds exploration incentives based on the trajectory. The authors report state-of-the-art from-scratch results over compared VLM baselines on 12 reward-free MetaWorld tasks, plus reward-free RL in three real-world experiments.
summary.zh: 论文提出VLMeg，用视觉语言模型作为具身强化学习的成功检测器，而非精确奖励回归器。方法根据当前回合与生成成功轨迹的相似度判断其是否适合评估，再从中选择混淆度最低的关键观测交由模型判断，并加入基于生成轨迹的探索激励。作者报告，在MetaWorld的12项无奖励任务中，该方法从零开始训练的表现超过所比较的VLM基线；另在3项真实世界实验中实现了无真实奖励的强化学习。
